newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada housing starts seen higher in 1997 and 1998.
newsitem.headline: Canada housing starts seen higher in 1997 and 1998.

text.p: Total housing starts in Canada are forecast to rise to 150,800 units this year and 159,200 in 1998, Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation said on Thursday.
The government agency said the expected rise in starts would mark a sharp increase over the 124,713 housing starts recorded in 1996.
CMHC said it expects starts of singled-detached homes to rise by 21 percent to 94,700 units in 1997, while multiple unit starts are expected to rise by 20 percent to 56,200.

Record sales on the existing homes market, low mortgage carrying costs, low inventories and employment growth are some of the reasons starts are expected to rise in 1997 and 1998 said Michel Laurence, senior economist with CMHC, in a statement.

CMHC made the projections in its second-quarter National Housing Outlook released on Thursday. In it the agency forecast the province of Alberta will have the most significant gain in new construction through 1998, bolstered by the strength of its resource and manufacturing economy. Alberta housing starts are seen rising from 16,665 in 1996 to 22,000 in 1997 and 24,600 in 1998.

Ontario will also see a large increase as the economy picks up momentum and inventories remain low, CMHC said. Housing starts in Ontario are expected to rise from 43,062 in 1996 to 58,000 in 1997 and 60,000 in 1998.
